question: The inputs are raw paired-end FASTQ files (6 samples, 3 treated vs 3 control, human liver) with no count matrix, but the sandbox has no read-alignment or transcript-quantification capability and no transcriptome/genome index to quantify against. Can you either (a) provide a gene-level count matrix (genes x 6 samples) plus the existing metadata.csv, or (b) have the environment provisioned with a quantifier (e.g. salmon/kallisto/STAR/HISAT2/Rsubread) together with a human GRCh38 transcriptome or genome index — which of these should I plan for?

input.questionContext: Verified against the environment: the CLI package track is empty (no salmon, kallisto, STAR, HISAT2, bowtie2, samtools, fastp, featureCounts, cutadapt), and no R aligner/counter is installed either (Rsubread, Rbowtie2, Rhisat2, QuasR all absent). Only post-quantification tooling exists — DESeq2 1.52.0, edgeR 4.10.3, limma 3.68.5, pydeseq2 0.5.4 — plus read-inspection libraries (ShortRead, Biostrings, pysam, Rsamtools), which can parse FASTQ but cannot align or pseudoalign at genome scale. The reference store holds the GENCODE v50 GRCh38 GTF and hg38 chrom sizes, but no transcriptome FASTA, no genome FASTA usable for indexing (only a PharmCAT-specific GRCh38.p13 bundle), and no prebuilt salmon/kallisto/STAR index. The sandbox also has no network access, so a script cannot fetch a reference or install a tool at run time. Consequently the FASTQ-to-counts step that the question ("which genes are differentially expressed between treated and control") depends on cannot be executed as provisioned; everything downstream (DESeq2 Wald test on 3 vs 3, LFC shrinkage, QC/PCA, pathway enrichment against the human WikiPathways GMT that IS present) is ready to run the moment counts exist.
